TITLE: PACCAR Q3 2026: trucks carry the quarter, 2027 rules weigh
COMPANY_INTRO: PACCAR designs and builds Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF heavy trucks, sells aftermarket parts and finances customers’ vehicles. Trucks were 76% of third-quarter truck and parts sales. Nasdaq-listed, market value around USD 55bn.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Truck pretax profit of USD 455m beat estimates by 43%, lifting net income 44% to USD 848m.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Reaction
TAKEAWAYS.text: Shares eased 0.6% on 27 October: EPS met consensus at USD 1.61, sales missed by 1.3%.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: Unfinalised 2027 emission penalties delay orders; supplier shortfalls held deliveries 4.5% below guidance.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 17.6x forward earnings, down from 23.9x in July while consensus EPS rose 3% over the same period.

H_P1: Earnings recover as the multiple falls
P1_PARAGRAPH: EPS of USD 1.61 met consensus and truck profit beat estimates by 43%, yet sales missed by 1.3% and the shares eased 0.6% on 27 October, a reaction in line with a mixed print. Higher deliveries lifted the truck pretax margin to 8.1%. The stock is held back by the unresolved 2027 emission rules and the timing of a pull-forward in orders.
C1_TITLE: PCAR: Q3 2026 results vs. consensus and guidance
C1_SUB: Surprise vs. pre-results consensus or analyst estimates, % · sales of truck, parts and other · deliveries vs. the ~42,000 company guide
C1_COMMENT: Trucks delivered a 43% profit surprise on revenue up 28% year on year, a pretax margin of 8.1%. Parts, the steadiest earner, posted record revenue of USD 1.78bn but pretax profit 14% below estimates. Supplier shortfalls cost about 1,900 deliveries against guidance, which we think explains most of the sales miss.
BASE_CASE: We keep the position. We underwrite consensus forward EPS of USD 5.90, 16% above a year ago and 34% below the 2023 peak, carried by truck margins and record Parts revenue. The debate has moved from the freight recession to the 2027 rules and the size of a pull-forward in orders. At 17.6x, the July premium is gone and sentiment is negative, which we think limits the downside. The next test is Q4 deliveries of 41,000 to 43,000, due in late January 2027.
UPSIDE: Final EPA non-conformance penalties before year-end that release held-back 2027 orders; Q4 deliveries at the top of the 41,000 to 43,000 range; a Q4 Truck, Parts and Other gross margin at 15%, the top of guidance.
DOWNSIDE: Q4 deliveries below 41,000, a sign that supplier constraints run into 2027; a gross margin below the 14% low end of guidance; a 2027 US and Canada market heading below 240,000 units if the pull-forward fails to materialise.
H_A1: Results: truck margins beat, parts slipped
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Consolidated revenue rose 19% to USD 7.94bn and net income 44% to USD 847.5m, or USD 1.61 per diluted share against USD 1.12 a year ago. Truck revenue grew 28% to USD 5.6bn on deliveries of 40,100, up 26%, which implies revenue per truck about 2% higher. Truck pretax profit reached USD 454.5m, a margin of 8.1%, against analyst estimates of USD 317m: operating leverage on higher volumes did the work. Parts revenue grew 3.2% to a record USD 1.78bn, but pretax profit of USD 404.4m, a 22.7% margin, came in 14% below estimates. Financial Services added USD 138.1m pretax, up 9.4%, on stable finance margins and a firmer used truck market.

Against consensus the print was mixed: EPS in line, sales 1.3% short at USD 7.38bn, truck profit ahead, Parts profit behind. The shares eased 0.6% on 27 October, a move in proportion to that mix, so surprise and reaction are aligned. The confirmed drivers are the delivery shortfall, which management attributed to supplier constraints, and an unchanged regulatory picture: customers are still waiting for the EPA’s non-conformance penalties before placing 2027 orders. We think the muted move reflects expectations that were already low: the stock fell 4.8% in the three sessions before the release and trades 25% below its July high.
H_A2: Outlook: Q4 recovers, 2027 hinges on rules
A2_PARAGRAPH: Management expects Q4 deliveries of 41,000 to 43,000 as supplier performance improves, a midpoint 5% above Q3, and a Truck, Parts and Other gross margin of 14% to 15%: price-cost is favourable, but production inefficiencies add cost. The 2026 US and Canada heavy truck market was narrowed to 240,000 to 260,000 units, and the first 2027 range of 240,000 to 280,000 has a midpoint 4% higher, supported by infrastructure-led vocational demand, where PACCAR holds a 40% share, and replacement. Europe is seen at 300,000 to 320,000 in both. Capital spending of USD 650m to 700m and research of USD 460m to 500m in 2027 fund clean-diesel, hybrid and battery-electric powertrains.
H_C2: Valuation: earnings up, the multiple derated
C2_TITLE: PCAR: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: PCAR US Equity, daily data resampled to weekly, from January 2011 · BEst 12m-forward consensus · 40-week simple MA · log scale · P/E shaded above (orange) / below (blue) its 2011 to 2026 average · last price is the 27 October close, after the release
C2_COMMENT: Over 12 months consensus forward EPS has risen 16.4% to USD 5.90 while the share price is up only 2.6%, so the multiple has done the adjusting. The derating is recent: at the 28 July peak of USD 138.2, after Q2, the stock traded on 23.9x; it now trades on 17.6x, the lowest since July 2025, 16% above the 15.1x average since 2011 and below the 20.9x one-year average. The price sits 13% below its 40-week average of USD 120. A 10% upgrade at an unchanged price would take the multiple to 16.0x, close to the long-run average.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, PACCAR results release of 27 October 2026, analyst research notes of 8 and 27 October 2026
